tools.name: start_service_request
tools.description: Start a new supported service request immediately with the user's full intent and known public facts. Returns the vertical introduction and next intake/matching step, including availability when intake is complete; no separate lookup is needed. Use provider_hint only for an explicitly named company.

tools.name: update_service_request
tools.description: Submit supplied answers and any chosen selected_time_key with the latest expected_state_version. Omitted optional/conditional fields do not block progress. tools.name: get_service_options
tools.description: Refresh availability only when needed, such as when the user asks to check again. start_service_request and update_service_request already return current matching data. Returns aggregated windows and refinement fields without selecting a company or reserving capacity.

tools.name: render_service_request_form
tools.description: Open the protected contact/terms/Confirm card only after company choice. tools.name: select_service_option
tools.description: Called only by the protected contact form after an explicit Confirm action. It rechecks the company already chosen in chat, creates a temporary hold and returns the protected contact session. Never use it to present a company picker or on card startup. It does not create a booking.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_service_booking" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: render_service_request_form, open_service_account · Private data: update_service_request, render_service_request_form, select_service_option · Public sink: update_service_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: render_service_request_form, open_service_account · Private data: update_service_request, render_service_request_form, select_service_option · Public sink: update_service_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "render_service_request_form" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
